deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S is a base scheme and X an S-scheme. On the previous page X is embedded in a smooth S-scheme Y, and Y^{ν+1} (the (ν+1)-fold fibre product over S) carries the diagonal embedding of X. For a sheaf F on X_cris, Grothendieck defines Zariski sheaves F^{(ν)} on X: on an open U ⊂ X, F^{(ν)}(U) is the value of F on the formal completion of V^{ν+1} along U, where V ⊂ Y is an open inducing U. Concretely this is lim_i F(U, U(i)^{ν+1}), the limit over the infinitesimal neighbourhoods of U. Under a quasi-coherence-type hypothesis on F, and first for X affine, these sheaves have no higher cohomology on affines. Together they form a cosimplicial sheaf ℱ^* (the Čech–Alexander construction).

Top of this page. Glueing over an affine cover gives H^*(X_cris, F) ≅ H^*(X_zar, ℱ^*), the hypercohomology of the associated complex. Hence there is a spectral sequence E_1^{p,q} = H^q(X, ℱ^{(p)}). The page's notation H^p(ν ↦ H^q(X, ℱ^{(ν)})) is really the E_2 term: the cosimplicial cohomology of the E_1 terms. It abuts to H^*(X_cris, F).

§6.3, special case. Let X_0 ⊂ X be a nilpotent closed immersion, and suppose F is the 'restriction' of a sheaf F_0 on X_{0,cris}, meaning F(U,T) = F_0(U ∩ X_0, T). Then X_0 also embeds in Y. Since X_0 and X have the same underlying space, the systems of infinitesimal neighbourhoods of X_0 and of X in Y^{ν+1} are mutually cofinal. So the formal completions Y^{ν+1}_{/X_0} and Y^{ν+1}_{/X} coincide, and ℱ^{(ν)} ≅ ℱ_0^{(ν)} as sheaves on X_zar = X_{0,zar}. The Čech–Alexander complexes therefore agree, giving H^*(X_cris, F) ≅ H^*(X_{0,cris}, F_0): nilpotent invariance.

Removing hypotheses. This was first proved for X globally embeddable in a smooth Y. Using an affine open cover and the cosimplicial/Čech argument removes the global-embedding hypothesis. He leaves open, in brackets, whether the quasi-coherence-type hypothesis on F can also be dropped.

Purpose. On the next page this is applied with X smooth over S, S_0 ⊂ S a nilpotent immersion and X_0 = X ×_S S_0. It shows that the de Rham cohomology of a smooth lifting depends only on X_0. In characteristic 0 this yields an intrinsic definition of de Rham cohomology for arbitrary (singular) X via the infinitesimal site. The site called 'cris' here is, in 1966-67 usage, essentially the infinitesimal site (no divided powers).
errors: The written arrow H^*(X_cris,F) ⟸ H^p(ν ↦ H^q(X,ℱ^{(ν)})) denotes a spectral sequence. The displayed term is properly the E_2 term (cohomology of the cosimplicial groups formed by the E_1 terms H^q(X,ℱ^{(ν)})). This is notational, not an error.

The nilpotent-invariance argument relies on the site having no divided-power condition: it is the infinitesimal site. For Berthelot's PD-crystalline site, invariance under an arbitrary nilpotent immersion X_0 ⊂ X is false in general without PD-compatibility conditions on the ideal of X_0. So the statement is correct only in the infinitesimal setting that 'cris' denoted at this date.

For the infinitesimal site the statement holds without any quasi-coherence hypothesis, because X_inf and X_{0,inf} are equivalent topoi when X_0 → X is a nilpotent closed immersion. The bracketed open question thus has a formal positive answer, which Grothendieck does not note here.

ideas.what: Computation of infinitesimal ('crystalline') cohomology by the cosimplicial sheaf of formal completions of Y^{ν+1} along X, with the associated spectral sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, IHES 1966, notes by Coates–Jussila); later Berthelot, Berthelot–Ogus for the PD case
ideas.where_published: Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968), 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes'

ideas.what: Invariance of infinitesimal cohomology under nilpotent immersions X_0 ⊂ X for sheaves coming from X_0
ideas.modern_name: Topological (nilpotent) invariance of the infinitesimal topos / infinitesimal cohomology
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés)

Question whether the quasi-coherence hypothesis on F can be dropped

deep.surprise_reason: These are working notes for Grothendieck's 1966 IHES crystals lectures. The Čech–Alexander computation and nilpotent invariance both appear in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés) and in later work by Berthelot and Hartshorne. The only open question on the page (dropping quasi-coherence) has a formal answer via equivalence of infinitesimal topoi.
